issues.description: The problem text instructs that the helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) should be public for easier testing, but both the provided template and the reference solution declare singFarmSongVerse as private. Additionally, the UML in the problem shows the method as private (negative sign) while the textual instruction asks for public — this internal contradiction in the problem statement plus the mismatch between spec and code can confuse students and lead to failing tests that expect the helper to be accessible.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (both UML and text) to require a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal) helper, or (B) change the template and solution to declare the helper as public (public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). Prefer option B if tests need to call the helper; ensure UML also shows it as public.

issues.description: The problem text specifies the helper method signature singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal), but the template currently declares singFarmSongVerse without a parameter (the Animal parameter is commented out). The reference solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The commented-out parameter in the template may mislead students about the required signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java to declare the helper with the exact signature required by the specification, e.g. public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (or at minimum include the Animal parameter in the template method signature if visibility is to remain private). This removes ambiguity and matches the expected implementation in the solution.
